step.rationale: Use the AcrylicBrush's authored tint and fallback as in-app acrylic because WinUI 3 removed HostBackdrop brushes. The property is removed in WinUI 3, so BackgroundSource="HostBackdrop" fails as WMC0011. AcrylicBrush itself still exists and still does in-app acrylic, so a use that only ever set BackgroundSource="Backdrop" can drop the attribute and keep working. HostBackdrop is the case that needs work; it is now a property of the window rather than of a brush, set as Window.SystemBackdrop = new DesktopAcrylicBackdrop(). That moves the decision out of XAML and into code, which is why this is a procedure and not a rename. Checked against the Windows App SDK materials and in-app acrylic documentation, and the open request to restore the property (microsoft-ui-xaml issue 9915) which confirms it is gone.

Use the AcrylicBrush's authored tint and fallback as in-app acrylic because WinUI 3 removed HostBackdrop brushes. The property is removed in WinUI 3, so BackgroundSource="HostBackdrop" fails as WMC0011. AcrylicBrush itself still exists and still does in-app acrylic, so a use that only ever set BackgroundSource="Backdrop" can drop the attribute and keep working. HostBackdrop is the case that needs work; it is now a property of the window rather than of a brush, set as Window.SystemBackdrop = new DesktopAcrylicBackdrop(). That moves the decision out of XAML and into code, which is why this is a procedure and not a rename. Checked against the Windows App SDK materials and in-app acrylic documentation, and the open request to restore the property (microsoft-ui-xaml issue 9915) which confirms it is gone.
